issues.detail: The Greek 'εδωκας' (did you give/hand over) is in the aorist tense, but the Vietnamese 'không giao' (did not hand over) combined with the context of the sentence implies a continuous action or a state. More importantly, the Greek 'εγώ ελθων' uses the participle 'ελθων' (coming), which functions as a temporal/circumstantial clause (when I come). The Vietnamese 'để khi ta đến' (so that when I come) adds a purposive/consecutive sense ('để') that is not present in the Greek.
The Greek 'αν επραξα αυτο' (if you did it / if you acted so) is entirely omitted in the Vietnamese translation. This is a significant conditional clause that qualifies the action of the debtor.
